headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks arise if MinerU ingests ai-engineering-hub outputs through shared MCP or files; no direct data-leak path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and file/API inputs, while ai-engineering-hub is tagged for agents/MCP/RAG. That creates a plausible bridge where content from A could be treated as instructions by B in default integrations. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU is connected to ai-engineering-hub outputs via MCP, shared files, or copy-paste automation
IF MinerU parses retrieved content as instructions rather than inert data
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Route A's outputs through a plain-text sanitizer before B reads them
Add provenance labels to all retrieved content
Require human review before any instruction-like text is executed
requires-engineering: implement content-type separation for instructions vs. data

B_data_leakage.rationale: A reports network_egress:none and no data classes touched, while B is documented as private/offline with read_filesystem:false and write_filesystem:false. The pair lacks evidence of shared sensitive data or an upload path, so leakage appears limited unless an external workspace or connector is added.
conditions: IF both agents are placed on a shared workspace with sensitive files
IF MinerU is configured to send extracted content to a remote endpoint outside its allowlist
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid placing secrets in any shared input directory
Verify MinerU's allowlist before enabling remote calls
Run a quick test with a harmless sample file
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or shell capabilities shown, and B cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is unlikely. The only notable overlap is B's concurrent inference, which does not create a write conflict with A.
conditions: IF A is extended with filesystem or git write permissions outside the profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through an external orchestrator
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets
Separate output directories per agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or folder
Check orchestrator locking before parallel runs
requires-engineering: add mutexes around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can transform PDFs and other documents into structured outputs, and ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG-oriented repository that could supply downstream content. If B consumes A's extracted text without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into later actions. No built-in verification step is evidenced, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as authoritative input to another agent or workflow
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks extracted facts before action
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checking for key fields
Sample-check a few extracted pages before use
Keep A's output labeled as machine-extracted
Block automatic action-taking from unverified extractions
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and validation rules

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is evidenced in either profile. A is docs-only with no touched data classes, and B is private/offline with no secrets handled, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF a deployment policy introduces retention or residency constraints not shown here
mitigations: Confirm data-class scope before deployment
Document retention settings for any shared workspace
Review residency requirements if regulated data is added
Keep regulated data out of this pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
